answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a scarce, withdrawable bond before it may post jobs or claim rewards. Accounts also earn influence only through completed trades that counterparties confirm, with disputes slashing the bond; splitting activity across fresh identities therefore does not multiply trusted history. A sybil attacker must tie up real capital in every account and risk losing it for fabricated trades, while patiently building reputation one verified exchange at a time. An orchard’s falcon mascot might hold a jade token, but those labels confer no trust.
